frameworks.name: Multi-Tier Distribution Strategy
frameworks.definition: A go-to-market approach that targets platform intermediaries (agencies/mentors) rather than end customers directly, increasing CAC efficiency through bulk onboarding and recurring revenue per intermediary.

frameworks.name: Four-Funnel CRM Architecture
frameworks.definition: A structured offer approach for online fitness coaches using four distinct funnels: mini-chat automation, link-in-bio lead magnet, application process, and conversion engine.

claims.text: Testing advertising campaigns requires spending at least 2x your target customer acquisition cost (CAC) to generate sufficient feedback cadence. Spending only your target CAC results in feedback so slow (one sale every two months) that you cannot determine if a campaign actually works. Alex Hormozi (Acquisition.com) applies this rule to all paid advertising channels.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Higher spend volume accelerates feedback frequency, enabling statistically significant iteration

numbers.axis: ad spend relative to target CAC

bounded_by: Does not apply to organic/free channels
Does not apply to campaigns with already-proven product-market fit

claims.text: When targeting end-users (online fitness coaches) with a B2B software offer, they will ask 'How do I get leads?' immediately after purchasing, creating an unexpected second sales/support burden. Positioning the offer to agencies/mentors who already have lead-generation capability avoids this secondary demand-generation problem.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: End-users default to asking for the distribution problem (leads) rather than just the product (software), shifting your role from vendor to distribution partner. Agencies already have lead flow and need operational leverage.
bounded_by: Does not apply to products that solve a standalone problem (e.g., accounting software)

claims.text: Agencies are 'one level up' from individual creators and offer superior unit economics: an agency can be acquired for ~$5,000 upfront, then pay $25,000 for onboarding, plus $1,000 per existing customer ($50,000 for 50 customers), plus 30% recurring revenue on top line. This is superior to direct creator targeting both for CAC and retention.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Agencies have existing customer relationships and cash flow to fund onboarding; creators do not. Recurring revenue multiplier comes from serving both the agency and their customer base.
bounded_by: Agencies must have existing customer base (40+ customers typical)
Does not apply to categories where end-user has independent monetization

claims.text: Marketing directly to SMBs (small businesses) with a software platform underperforms compared to marketing to agencies serving those SMBs. Alex Hormozi (Acquisition.com) experienced this when comparing Go High Level direct-to-coach positioning versus agency-to-coach positioning.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: target market is small businesses or creators
claims.mechanism: Agencies have existing customer relationships, payment capability, and operational trust; individual SMBs/creators have none of these.
bounded_by: Assumes the intermediate (agency) layer exists and has healthy margins

claims.text: For targeting online fitness coaches, the primary pain point is converting Instagram followers into customers without spending all day in direct messages. Coaches are Instagram-native (primary channel), not LinkedIn-native. A CRM that solves 'turn followers to customers via automation' addresses the most acute point of friction in their workflow.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: online fitness coaches as target market
bounded_by: Does not apply to coaches using LinkedIn or email as primary channel
Does not apply to offline training (in-person personal training)

claims.text: Using multiple diverse customer avatars (different body types, ethnicities, ages, niches) in case studies makes the offer feel more universally applicable and reduces the prospect's concern 'Will this work for someone like me?' A fitness CRM demonstrated across 5 coaches—bodybuilder, vegan athlete, Asian powerlifter, 50+ woman—shows wider applicability than a single-niche case study.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: target market has visible psychographic diversity
prospect concerns center on 'fit for my niche'
claims.mechanism: Diverse avatars in case studies reduce ingroup/outgroup perception and allow each prospect to self-identify with at least one case study

numbers.axis: number of diverse avatars in case studies

bounded_by: Avatars must be authentic case studies, not representative generics

claims.text: Converting a product-as-individual-guru positioning (coaching/mentorship) to product-as-software positioning requires different messaging. The prospect cares about outcomes (e.g., recurring revenue from customers) rather than the guru's expertise. Focus messaging on the customer retention and revenue stability benefits rather than the tool's features.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: transitioning from guru/mentorship positioning to SaaS positioning

claims.text: Retention improved from 'terrible' to good by building a better product. The speaker's fitness coaching CRM improved retention through product design changes; this enabled scaling from $2M annual revenue toward $1M monthly without increasing CAC proportionally.
claims.speaker: Go High Level Fitness Coaching Platform Founder

claims.text: When serving a two-sided marketplace (agencies and their customers), your organization must have dedicated customer success resources for each layer: a customer success manager for the agencies (first tier) and separate customer success for end-users (second tier). The two-sided structure creates distinct support needs.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Offering a value proposition that solves a customer's specific problem (e.g., 'turn followers to customers via automation') is more effective than requiring the customer to solve their own demand generation first (e.g., 'get leads on your own, then we'll help you convert'). You must meet customers who have the problem to solve; you don't want to generate demand, you want to channel existing demand.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: target market has independent demand generation challenges
claims.mechanism: Demand channeling (solving for existing customer needs) scales faster than demand generation (creating new problems to solve)

examples.text: Alex Hormozi ran a Go High Level-like platform (with Alan) targeting SMB agencies. When they tried marketing directly to SMBs, conversion was poor. They pivoted to marketing to agencies—Cairo Agency, other established agencies—offering a platform to handle customer fulfillment. The agencies retained them longer despite lower margin because they received recurring revenue from customers rather than having to generate new customers themselves. The model succeeded by offering agencies a way to increase customer lifetime value (stickiness) without requiring the agencies to acquire more customers.

For online fitness coaches on Instagram with fewer than 5,000 followers, the Go High Level CRM enables 5 new client acquisitions per week through automation. The coaches are concerned that the tool won't work for their niche or follower count. Case studies showing 5 different coaches with similar low follower counts (jacked bodybuilder, vegan athlete, Asian powerlifter, 50+ woman, etc.) each achieving 5 clients/week demonstrate that the tool works across diverse niches and body types, reducing the prospect's 'will this work for me' concern.

An online fitness coaching CRM company is stuck at $2M annual revenue and wants to reach $1M monthly. They've improved product retention (was 'terrible', now 'good'), have solid LTV ($9k) and CAC ratio (4.6:1), and have three reliable customer acquisition channels: strategic partnerships with fitness mentors, organic growth, and Meta ads. However, Meta ads are underfunded ($2k/month) and the company is uncertain about messaging—they're positioning as a software/automation tool, but coaches/mentors expect 'guru' positioning with personal guidance.

practices.text: When running paid advertising tests, allocate 2x your target CAC to the campaign before declaring it successful or unsuccessful. This ensures sufficient feedback cadence to distinguish signal from noise.
Use multiple diverse customer avatars (different ages, ethnicities, body types, niches) in case studies to demonstrate that an offer works across different customer psychographs.
Prepare messaging that emphasizes customer outcomes (recurring revenue, customer retention, business stability) rather than tool features when selling to other coaches/mentors.
When serving both agencies and end-customers, staff dedicated customer success for each tier rather than trying to manage both with a single team.

Test messaging hooks on your target market to discover which value prop resonates: 'aren't you tired of losing customers every 3 months?' vs. 'imagine if every customer from your entire career still paid you' vs. 'what if you had recurring revenue that actually stuck year-over-year?'
